sections.h2: Where is the Warren County, NC tax office and how do you pay?
sections.html:
The tax office is at 117 S. Main St., Warrenton, NC 27589, next door to the Warren County Courthouse. The mailing address is Warren County Tax Office, PO Box 240, Warrenton, NC 27589. The office observes most national holidays.

The county lists four ways to pay. Fees apply to some of them, so the free routes are worth knowing.

  • By phone at 1-866-483-9680 or online at warren.webtaxpay.com. The county prints debit card at $3.95, credit card at 2.60 percent of the amount charged, and check or eCheck at $2.50.
  • By mail to the PO Box above, which carries no fee.
  • In the drop box to the right of the tax office front door, also free.

The tax administrator is responsible to the Board of County Commissioners and also to the County Manager, the state Department of Revenue and the Property Tax Commission, according to the county page.

sections.h2: What is the Warren County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The Tax Administrator page lists a county rate for real and personal property of $0.5950 per one hundred dollars for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. Warren County's budget documents have shown other figures during budget season, so ask the tax office to confirm the rate for your bill before you rely on it.

The county page says its latest revaluation was in 2025 and that the 2025 assessments stay on the books until 2032, unless an owner adds a garage, a room or a new house on a vacant lot. The next county revaluation is scheduled to take effect in 2033, and Warren contracts with a private appraisal company to help with the work.

That long cycle shapes a sale. Between revaluations, a buyer's tax value stays tied to the 2025 appraisal, not to the price in your contract, unless the new owner changes the building.

sections.h2: When are Warren County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1, and the county says 2026 taxes do not become delinquent until January 6, 2027, with January 5, 2027 the last day to pay without interest. After that the county charges 2 percent for January and an additional three-fourths of one percent each month.

The county's calendar spells out the steps after the due date, and it is worth reading if you are behind.

Warren County tax calendar from the Tax Administrator and Important Tax Dates pages
WhenWhat happens
January 1Ownership and value fixed for the tax year; real property appeal period opens
January 6Interest begins on unpaid bills; enforced collections, up to foreclosure, begin after this date
January 31Last day of the listing period; 10 percent penalty for late listing
March and AprilDelinquent letters mailed in March; unpaid accounts advertised in the local paper in April
June 1Age exemption, disabled veteran and disability relief applications due
AugustAnnual tax bills mailed
September 1Current year taxes due

sections.h2: Can you close a deed in Warren County with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
Not without a tax certification or a closing attorney's statement. The county says that effective January 7, 2026, the Board of Commissioners adopted by resolution G.S. 161-31, which requires the Register of Deeds to refuse a deed transferring real property unless the Tax Collector has certified that no delinquent taxes are a lien on the property.

There is one way around the certification: the closing attorney can add a statement to the deed that all delinquent taxes will be paid at closing. Deeds that need the certification must be presented to the Tax Collector's office between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., so staff can research the property and apply a certification stamp if it is warranted.

For a seller, the practical lesson is to check the tax account before the closing date. A house with several unpaid years can still sell, but the arrears have to be paid from proceeds, and the tax collector needs time to research the parcel.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Warren County property value?
sections.html:
Real property appeals open every January 1 and run until the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The county says the 2026 real property appeal period ended May 18, 2026, when the board adjourned, and the 2027 process begins January 1, 2027. A 2027 informal appeal form is posted in the county's Forms section.

State law says the board first meets no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May. A taxpayer asks for a hearing before the board adjourns. If the board rules against you, notice of appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mailed its decision.

Two rules from the county page matter for real property. The burden of proof falls on the taxpayer to show a substantial overstatement of value, and appeals cannot rest on current market values unless it is a revaluation year. For personal property such as vehicles, boats, trailers, aircraft and business equipment, the appeal window is 30 days from receiving the tax bill, which serves as the notice of value.

sections.h2: What listing and present use value rules apply in Warren County?
sections.html:
Personal and business personal property must be listed every January 1 through 31, and a late listing carries a 10 percent penalty. The county's list of items includes single wide mobile homes, farm equipment, unregistered vehicles, boats and motors, aircraft, billboards and short-term rentals, among others.

Real property is permanently listed in Warren County, so owners do not relist each year unless they changed something. Extension requests must be made by January 31, and mailed listings must be postmarked by that date, or by April 15 if an extension was granted. The county suggests getting a mailing receipt from the post office.

Warren is a rural county, and the present use value program matters to landowners with working land. The county page sets these minimums:

  • Agricultural land: at least ten acres in commercial production of crops or animals.
  • Forest land: at least twenty acres meeting the forest requirements.
  • Horticultural land: at least five acres in commercial production of fruits, vegetables, nursery or floral products.
  • Agricultural and horticultural income: an average gross of $1,000 per year over three years; forest land has no income test.

Applications are due January 31. A buyer of PUV land must apply within sixty days of the transfer, so a seller should tell the buyer's attorney the parcel is enrolled.

sections.h2: What property tax relief is available in Warren County?
sections.html:
State programs for older, disabled and veteran owners are available, with applications due June 1. The county says seniors 65 and over can pick up an application starting January 2, and applicants for disability or disabled veteran relief need the state forms A-9A or NCDVA-9 along with the application.

State law sets the terms. The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value, and the Department of Revenue lists a 2026 income limit of $38,800. The disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000, with no age or income test. A person receives benefit from only one of the three programs. The county's own page also describes present use value savings as up to 90 percent for eligible landowners.

If you inherited a Warren County house, ask the tax office whether the previous owner's exclusion continues; relief generally does not pass to a new owner without a fresh application.

faqs.q: When does Warren County charge interest on property tax?
faqs.a: January 6. The county says 2026 taxes are not delinquent until January 6, 2027, and January 5 is the last day to pay without interest. The rate is 2 percent for January and three-fourths of one percent each month after.

faqs.q: Does Warren County require a tax certification to record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes, since a January 7, 2026 resolution under G.S. 161-31. The Register of Deeds will not accept a deed unless the Tax Collector certifies no delinquent taxes are a lien, or the closing attorney adds a statement that delinquent taxes will be paid at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Warren County property tax without a fee?
faqs.a: By mail to PO Box 240, Warrenton, NC 27589, or in the drop box beside the tax office door at 117 S. Main St. The county lists card and eCheck payments with fees.

faqs.q: When was Warren County last revalued?
faqs.a: 2025. The county says those assessments remain on the books until 2032 unless improvements change them, and the next revaluation is scheduled to take effect in 2033.

faqs.q: Is the Warren County tax appeal period open?
faqs.a: The 2026 real property appeal period ended May 18, 2026, when the Board of Equalization and Review adjourned. The 2027 appeal process begins January 1, 2027.
